title: Stickler Syndrome: The Collagens of Ocular Pathology
summary: Stickler syndrome is the most common autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder in Europe, characterized by a triad of ocular, orofacial, and skeletal manifestations. It arises from mutations in collagen genes leading to distinct vitreoretinal degeneration and systemic risk.

sections.title: Definition & Molecular Etiology
sections.content: Stickler syndrome (Hereditary Progressive Arthro-Ophthalmopathy) is a multisystem disorder of collagen Type II, IX, and XI. Primary mutations involve COL2A1 (Type 1), COL11A1 (Type 2), or COL11A2 (Type 3). Pathophysiology centers on aberrant collagen fibrillogenesis, disrupting the integrity of the vitreous gel, joint cartilage, and inner ear structures.

rows: High risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD)

branches: Pierre Robin Sequence (Micrognathia, Glossoptosis, Cleft Palate)

sections.title: Red Flags: Ocular Emergencies
content: Sudden onset of photopsia or peripheral visual field defect (Retinal Detachment risk ~50%)
Giant retinal tears (GRT) occur at the vitreous base interface
Bilateral involvement requires prophylactic 360-degree retinal cryotherapy or laser

rows: Severe midfacial hypoplasia, accelerated skeletal maturation
Ectopia lentis, aortic root dilation, systemic laxity

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Baseline dilated fundus exam + slit lamp biomicroscopy.
Step 2: Annual retinal surveillance by vitreoretinal specialist.
Step 3: Prophylactic laser photocoagulation for at-risk lattice-like degeneration.
Step 4: Surgical management of RRD: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) + silicone oil/gas tamponade.
Step 5: Pediatric cardiology/ENT referral for systemic syndromic monitoring.

content.explanation: S: Skeletal (early OA), T: Type II Collagen, I: Inherited (AD), C: Cleft palate, K: Knees (joint pain), L: Large eyes (high myopia), E: Ear (hearing loss), R: Retinal Detachment.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Vitreous appearance is 'optically empty' in Type 1.
High incidence of retinal detachment in first two decades.
Avoid unnecessary ocular trauma (contact sports counseling).
Counsel on 50% recurrence risk for offspring (Autosomal Dominant).

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent evidence supports early prophylactic 360-degree laser retinopexy in patients with type 1 Stickler syndrome to reduce RRD rate from ~50% to <5%. Genetic counseling via NGS (Next-Gen Sequencing) panels is now standard of care to differentiate Type 1 from Type 2 and 3, allowing for personalized prognostic counseling.
